units.text: Build a new, independently deployed Meri workspace with the Claude Agent SDK, AI Elements, governed Capiro data and memory access, browser work, downloadable artifacts, and durable execution. Codex coordinates implementation, delegates bounded work sessions to Hermes, verifies the resulting commits, and owns integration and deployment. Hermes is a development worker; it is not part of Meri's production agent runtime.

units.text: This plan implements the defined first release in the updated Meri Greenfield Agent Plan. A runnable demo is a milestone, not release acceptance. Expect roughly two weeks for a demo, six to eight weeks for a controlled pilot, and ten to fourteen weeks for production readiness with three senior engineers and part-time platform/QA support. These are planning estimates; credentials, source access, policy discovery, and qualification can change them. Full parity with every current Meri business workflow is a separately estimated scope.

units.text: The inspected design baseline contains 85 main frames, including five state boards; 29 overlays; 60 state examples; 15 reusable component families; and 11 named walkthrough entry points. It covers the defined standalone v1 UI capability families. Those counts describe designs, not implemented features or full parity with current Meri. The file remains editable: at W00, record the actual Figma revision or available version identifier, capture date, frame IDs and reference screenshots. Keep that snapshot in the repository so later design edits cannot silently change an active ticket's acceptance criteria.

units.text: Figma specifies layout, typography, component appearance, navigation, dialogs and representative states. Next.js/React and AI Elements provide the executable UI. Backend/event contracts specify real state transitions, authorization and outcomes. Prototype navigation is an example, not an API specification or evidence that the SDK implements the corresponding behavior. Generated Figma snippets may accelerate layout work after review; do not ship a screenshot-based UI or generated code without adopted components, real events and acceptance checks.

units.text: Implement the generic patterns with AI Elements and shadcn/ui primitives before writing custom UI. Map Conversation/Message/PromptInput to streaming chat; Plan/Task/Queue/Tool to run activity; Sources/InlineCitation to authorized evidence; Confirmation to governed approval; Artifact/Attachments/FileTree to files; and Context/Checkpoint/WebPreview/CodeBlock/Terminal to their applicable workspace views. Use one application event adapter to the SDK. Adopt existing preview and authoring libraries from this plan rather than building Office editors. units.text: This R2 plan and its companion updated capability workbook are the current two-file deployment handoff. They retain the defined first-release scope; any already-provided Meri Greenfield Agent Plan remains background for unaffected requirements. Agents do not need to obtain a third document to start the REL work. A runnable demo is a milestone, not release acceptance. Expect roughly two weeks for a demo, six to eight weeks for a controlled pilot, and ten to fourteen weeks for production readiness with three senior engineers and part-time platform/QA support. These are inherited planning assumptions, not a certification that R2 preserves the remaining schedule. Re-estimate from accepted deployment work, the added named-skill qualification, credentials, source access, policy discovery and qualification results at W00. Full parity with every current Meri business workflow is a separately estimated scope.

Original request and newly shortened authority deadlines form one shrink-only live cutoff through pool acquisition, transaction setup, reserve, marker and automatic settlement; late COMMIT remains uncertain and cleanup is still required. units.text: This R2 plan and its companion updated capability workbook are the current two-file deployment handoff. They retain the defined first-release scope; any already-provided Meri Greenfield Agent Plan remains background for unaffected requirements. Agents do not need to obtain a third document to start the REL work. A runnable demo is a milestone, not release acceptance. Expect roughly two weeks for a demo, six to eight weeks for a controlled pilot, and ten to fourteen weeks for production readiness with three senior engineers and part-time platform/QA support. These are inherited planning assumptions, not a certification that R2 preserves the remaining schedule. Re-estimate from accepted deployment work, the added named-skill qualification, credentials, source access, policy discovery and qualification results at W00. Full parity with every current Meri business workflow is a separately estimated scope.
